requirement: Describe a Phase 2, randomized, double-blind, parallel, placebo-controlled study in PCR-confirmed adults who are asymptomatic or have mild COVID-19.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the study population and design.

requirement: Specify 1:1 simple randomization balanced by treatment and gender, with allocation implemented by an unblinded pharmacist and identical active/placebo tablets.

evidence.text: The protocol describes the randomization and masking procedures.

notes: The phrase simple randomization balanced by treatment and gender needs operational clarification before implementation.

requirement: Compare ivermectin 12 mg daily for three days plus paracetamol 500 mg four times daily for 14 days against matching ivermectin placebo plus the same paracetamol regimen.

evidence.text: The protocol gives both treatment regimens.

requirement: Report 66 randomized subjects, with protocol-stated 80% power and 95% confidence, while flagging that the source gives no assumed control rate, effect size, alpha formulation or attrition calculation.

evidence.text: The sample-size section provides only total size, power and confidence.

notes: Do not invent the event-rate assumptions.

requirement: Define the Day-14 primary endpoint as the proportion without progression to severe COVID-19.

evidence.text: The protocol states the primary disease-control endpoint and Day-14 contrast.

requirement: Classify severe progression when any criterion occurs: respiratory rate at least 30/min, resting oxygen saturation at most 93%, or respiratory failure, mechanical ventilation, septic shock or non-respiratory organ failure.

evidence.text: The protocol lists the severe-progression criteria.

requirement: Preserve randomized treatment assignment for withdrawals and severe progressions and count them as primary treatment failures; do not replace dropouts.

evidence.text: The protocol assigns all listed withdrawal cases to their original arm as treatment failures and disallows replacement.

requirement: Compare the frequency of mild-to-severe disease progression between randomized groups using a chi-square test at two-sided nominal p<0.05 and report group proportions with 95% confidence intervals.

evidence.text: The SAP specifies chi-square, nominal significance and categorical 95% confidence intervals.

notes: The source does not specify the confidence-interval construction or small-cell fallback.

requirement: Evaluate SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR viral-load or Ct change over selection, Day 5 and Day 14, daily symptom presence/frequency through Day 14, comorbidities, BCG history and COVID-19 death.

evidence.text: The protocol lists secondary objectives, timings and variables.

requirement: For secondary quantitative comparisons use group t tests only after distribution assessment, summarize categorical outcomes with frequencies and chi-square, and label Pearson correlations and linear regressions as exploratory rather than confirmatory.
acceptable_values: t test for quantitative group comparisons

evidence.text: The short SAP lists tests and exploratory analyses.

requirement: Ask whether the protocol's as-randomized failure rule applies to every withdrawal and missing Day-14 assessment and how to handle intermittent missing viral-load and symptom data; do not substitute the SAP's vague at-least-two-visits complete-case rule.

evidence.text: The protocol calls listed withdrawals treatment failures.
The SAP includes subjects completing at least two visits and says ITT only if deemed appropriate.

notes: This unresolved population contradiction is central to expert review.

requirement: Summarize AEs and SAEs by randomized group during 14 days and continue weekly safety/symptom follow-up after Day 14 until disease resolution for unresolved subjects.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies safety endpoints and extended follow-up.

requirement: Clarify the safety population and treatment attribution because the SAP says all patients receiving at least one ivermectin dose, which could incorrectly exclude placebo recipients.
acceptable_values: include both randomized arms with at least one assigned dose

evidence.text: The literal safety-population wording mentions only patients receiving ivermectin.

notes: A statistician must resolve the wording before executable use.

requirement: Ask whether any multiplicity control or endpoint hierarchy applies across the primary and numerous secondary analyses; absent confirmation, label secondary p-values exploratory.

evidence.text: The SAP applies p<0.05 broadly but states no multiplicity procedure.

requirement: Correctly identify and request adjudication of the malformed null hypothesis, which names ivermectin plus paracetamol for both groups even though the randomized control is placebo plus paracetamol; also confirm the estimand, contrast direction, effect measure, CI method and small-cell test.

evidence.text: The null repeats ivermectin for both groups while the alternative and treatment section identify placebo control.
The SAP says only chi-square for progression frequency.
